the synthesis of all stereoisomers of the amide and its precursor, methyl ester.

all four stereoisomer of tryptoline have a significant cytotoxic activity on HeLa cell line.

A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the 1S,3S,9S isomer of the tryptoline derivative is the most potent cytotoxic compound.
the (2S,3R,4S,9S)-isomer of 1-(p-methoxyphenyl)tetrahydro-β -carboline-3-carboxylate (1) is the most active compound, whereas the (2S,3R,4R,9R )-isomer of 3-carboxamide (2) was the least active.

The main takeaway from our work is that
the stereochemistry at the C-3 carbon of the tetrahydro-ß-carboline skeleton is a critical factor for cell viability.
the stereochemistry at position 2 and 3 of the tryptoline molecule has a clear impact on the biological properties of the molecule.
the (R)-enantiomer of the tryptoline is the most cytotoxic, whereas the (S)-enantiomer is the least toxic.
